findings.issue: Springer permits limited drafting of literature reviews and summaries, analysis assistance, and human verification; it disallows writing an entire manuscript or AI interpretation. This remains conditional and compatible with the specified human-led workflow.
findings.resolution: Retain AI policy and its restrictions; check current journal-specific disclosure wording before submission.

findings.issue: Journal explicitly states no submission or publication fees and encourages submissions from all countries; Sage prohibits AI analysis of experiences and themes and gives a disclosure rule for generated text without clearly affirming substantive manuscript drafting.
findings.resolution: Retain verified-free and international geography, but keep AI compatibility unclear pending affirmative drafting evidence.

findings.issue: A previous-publisher 2023 acceptance rate is historical, not current Cambridge acceptance odds.
findings.resolution: Retain with its year, previous-publisher label and final-decision population; do not portray as current.

findings.issue: The fee audit identifies unresolved page-charge language alongside the no-fee statement.
findings.resolution: Keep total author costs unverified until applicability is resolved.

notes: Reviewed all 17 IDs and the complete fee, geography and AI-policy output sets. Official current journal pages independently confirm the 2025 Scientometrics impact factors and Oxford journal metrics for Research Evaluation and Science and Public Policy; all previously sourced values preserved with their periods and definitions.

Sage policy directly reviewed: permitted literature and code support do not by themselves establish substantive drafting, and the disclosure clause alone is not permission. Sage metrics endpoints for the four newly discovered journals were inaccessible in the browser; no invented figures added.

Metrics are journal-level context, not an individual submission acceptance probability. Official indexed Taylor & Francis metrics were previously recorded with direct-page 403 caveat; historical Cambridge rate remains explicitly historical. Independent review is not human scientific review.
